title: Count the day the way the network counts it

blocks.text: An acquirer's switch sends its totals in an `0500` every evening, and the network answers `2`, out of balance, on most days, even on days when the network's settlement report pays exactly what the switch expected.

`DayTotals.count` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/DayTotals.java` reads one day's journal and returns the totals the `0500` carries. Its journal holds purchases and refunds (processing code `20`), authorizations, and reversals of purchases and of refunds, with their repeats. The comment above `count` says what an entry holds.

Finish the three methods marked `TODO` so that the switch counts the day the way the network does. `add` holds the switch's current counting, which is what makes the network answer `2`. About 20 lines in total.

cases.says: approved purchases are counted and summed as debits, approved refunds as credits
a declined purchase or refund moved nothing, so it counts nowhere
an approved 0100 is counted as an authorization and never as a debit
an 0420 and its 0421 repeats name one original in DE 90 and count once
a reversal is counted in the reversal fields and does not take its purchase off the debits
the reversal of a refund is a credit reversal
entries whose DE 15 is another business day are left out
an acknowledged reversal counts although it carries no DE 39

origin.section: 19.3. Both Ends Count the Day by the Same Rules, and a Reversal Is Counted in Fields of Its Own

concepts: A day's totals count only that day's approved requests and acknowledged reversals, keep authorizations out of the money fields, and count each reversal once, in fields of its own, without taking its original off.
